Apuñalamiento en Times Square: Vicepresidenta de Bank of America muere tras ataque en Nueva York
Piacenti, residente en Nueva Jersey, trabajaba como vicepresidenta de la sección de Negocios y Conflictos en Bank of America, cuyas oficinas se encuentran a solo una manzana del lugar del ataque en Times Square.
Nueva York, Estados Unidos/Erin Piacenti, de 32 años, fue apuñalada por una mujer con problemas de salud mental en plena luz del día. La policía abatió a la atacante tras negarse a soltar los cuchillos.
Un apuñalamiento en Times Square dejó como saldo una mujer muerta y otra herida de gravedad este lunes en el corazón de Nueva York. La víctima mortal fue identificada como Erin Piacenti, una vicepresidenta de Bank of America de 32 años que hacía poco había celebrado su segundo aniversario de boda.
El ataque fue protagonizado por Pamela Cisneros, una residente de Queens de 49 años con conocidos problemas de salud mental. Según las autoridades, Cisneros extrajo dos cuchillos grandes de una bolsa y comenzó a amenazar a los transeúntes a plena luz del día en la turística zona.
La agresión fue rápida y letal. Primero, la sospechosa se acercó a un hombre de 68 años y lo apuñaló en el abdomen. Veinte segundos después, atacó a Erin Piacenti, quien también recibió una puñalada en el abdomen que finalmente le causó la muerte. El hombre de 68 años permanece en condición estable en un hospital.
Piacenti, residente en Nueva Jersey, trabajaba como vicepresidenta de la sección de Negocios y Conflictos en Bank of America, cuyas oficinas se encuentran a solo una manzana del lugar del ataque en Times Square. Un portavoz de la entidad bancaria señaló que estaban profundamente tristes por la trágica pérdida de su extraordinaria compañera.
El Departamento de Policía de Nueva York respondió de inmediato. La comisionada Jessica Tisch detalló que los agentes intentaron dialogar con Cisneros durante cuatro minutos para que soltara las armas. La atacante respondió que no soltaría nada y que prefería matar a los dos, antes de abalanzarse contra los oficiales.
Tras fallar un intento de inmovilizarla con una pistola eléctrica, los agentes dispararon sus armas de fuego. Cisneros fue trasladada a un hospital, donde fue declarada muerta.
El alcalde Zohran Mamdani confirmó los hechos en una rueda de prensa, expresando su profunda tristeza por la pérdida de la víctima y el fallecimiento de la presunta autora. Por su parte, la policía descartó cualquier vínculo con el terrorismo, calificando el suceso como una situación extraordinariamente peligrosa.
Datos tomados de AFP y La Vanguardia.

The Ivy League-educated banker fatally stabbed in Times Square was a new mother who had only recently returned from maternity leave after celebrating her baby daughter’s baptism, according to online posts.
Erin Piacenti, 32, a University of Pennsylvania graduate from Chester, New Jersey, shared a joyful photo just four days before she was killed, showing her smiling while holding her infant beside her husband, the New York Times reported.
Piacenti, who also graduated from Fordham Law School and later built a career at Bank of America, wrote that she felt grateful to have spent five months at home caring for her newborn daughter, according to the report.
Fordham Law School in the Bronx mourned her death in a statement, saying, “We are heartbroken to learn of the tragic and senseless loss of our alumna, Erin (Guiltinan) Piacenti.”
In her post, Piacenti reflected on her daughter’s recent baptism and the travels she and her husband had enjoyed after marking their second wedding anniversary, including trips to Long Beach, New Jersey, Maine and Rhode Island.
Her grandmother remembered Piacenti to the Times as a “beautiful, beautiful girl.”
The Bank of America executive was stabbed to death Monday afternoon in a random attack in Manhattan’s theater district by Pamela Cisneros, 49, a mother of three described as mentally disturbed. Cisneros also stabbed and injured another passerby before police shot her dead.

“We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague,” Bank of America said in a statement about Piacenti, who attended Villa Walsh Academy, a private Catholic girls’ school in Morristown, New Jersey, before continuing on to an elite education and professional career.

“She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. Our hearts go out to her family and all of her loved ones,’’ the banking giant said.
“Erin and her husband, Frank, graduated in 2021 and have been cherished members of the Fordham Law family.
“During this devastating time, our thoughts, prayers, and deepest sympathies are with Frank, their families, and all who knew and loved Erin.”

SAVAGE knife attack in Times Square ends with LETHAL police confrontation caught on video
September 01, 2026
Police said the attack was 'unprovoked and random.'
New York City police gunned down a woman who had attacked random strangers with a knife in Times Square on Monday.
Cellphone video captured the moment that police surrounded the woman, who lunged at them while armed with two knives.
Police were able to recover two knives at the scene.
Police said the 49-year-old woman began the "unprovoked and random" knife attack on strangers near 41st Street and Seventh Avenue.
She allegedly stabbed a 68-year-old man in his abdomen as the victim walked out of the subway with his wife. He was hospitalized for treatment of his injuries.
A second victim was identified as 32-year-old Erin Piacenti of Chester, New Jersey, who died of her injuries.
Witnesses flagged down officers who confronted the woman for about four minutes.
The officers "gave her numerous commands to drop the knife," said NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch.
"During the encounter, she told the officers, 'I'm not dropping anything. I would rather kill both of you.' She repeated, 'I will kill you,'" Tisch added.
Officers deployed Tasers, and other officers shot at the woman, which can be viewed on the graphic cellphone video.
She was hospitalized and later declared dead, Tisch said.
The woman was later identified as Pamela Cisneros of Queens, who had a documented history of mental illness, according to Tisch. She added that police were able to recover two knives at the scene.

Piacenti worked as a vice president at Bank of America.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) thanked police at the media briefing.
"I want to thank the NYPD officers who stepped in and prevented a horrific attack from becoming even worse," the mayor said. "This is what the men and women of this department do every single day to keep our city safe."
He added that body-camera footage from police would be released after an investigation.

Eyewitness video captured the chaos after a woman stabbed two strangers in Times Square within roughly 20 seconds, killing one, before police spent four minutes trying to persuade her to drop two knives.
The sharply different timelines define the deadly Monday attack. Police said Pamela Cisneros, 49, moved from one victim to the next in seconds. Officers later surrounded her near an NYPD substation and repeatedly ordered her to surrender before Tasers failed and she charged at them with both knives. Two officers then opened fire.
Two stabbings in 20 seconds
The attack began at about 4:24 p.m. near West 41st Street and Seventh Avenue, according to an Associated Press account of NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch’s briefing.
Tisch said Cisneros pulled two large kitchen knives from a red shopping bag and stabbed a 68-year-old man in the abdomen as he waited to cross the street with his wife. Cisneros then moved north and stabbed 32-year-old Erin Piacenti in the abdomen. Police said the two apparently random attacks occurred about 20 seconds apart.
This lady was running around stabbing people in time square. She straight up stabbed the person in front of me. Shit could’ve been me pic.twitter.com/lYfye4J1t1
— 𝖠𝖴𝖲𝖳𝖤𝖭꩜ (@austen_tv) August 31, 2026
Four-minute police talkdown
Witnesses pointed officers toward Cisneros as she continued up Seventh Avenue. Police surrounded her between West 42nd and West 43rd streets, where Tisch said officers spent about four minutes talking to her and giving her numerous commands to drop the knives.
“I’m not dropping anything. I would rather kill both of you. I will kill you,” Cisneros says in the video.
Multiple officers then fired their Tasers, but Cisneros remained standing. Video shows her swing both arms and rush toward officers with a knife in each hand. Two officers fired their service weapons and struck her.
Today in Times Square when tasers don’t work pic.twitter.com/aALVDZgYD0
— The E Man🇺🇸Street PHD (@DETECTIVE4LIFE) August 31, 2026
Officers immediately handcuffed Cisneros and began first aid. Emergency crews took her to Bellevue Hospital, where doctors pronounced her dead.
Bank executive killed
Paramedics took both stabbing victims to Bellevue Hospital. Doctors pronounced Piacenti dead, while the 68-year-old man remained in stable condition.
Reuters reported that Piacenti worked in Bank of America’s business selection and conflicts unit. The bank called her a valued teammate and expressed condolences to her family.
Police rule out terrorism
Tisch said investigators had no reason to believe the attack involved terrorism. Police described both stabbings as random and unprovoked.
Cisneros had no NYPD arrest record but had a documented mental health history involving previous police encounters, Tisch said. Officials did not disclose the nature of those encounters.
The NYPD released an image of the two knives recovered at the scene. The department’s Force Investigation Division continues to investigate the police shooting, and officials said the NYPD will release officers’ body-camera footage.
